text: Nearly all the wisdom we possess, that is to say, true and sound wisdom, consists of two parts: the knowledge of God and of ourselves.
author: John Calvin

text: Man's nature, so to speak, is a perpetual factory of idols.
author: John Calvin

text: We are not our own: let not our reason nor our will, therefore, sway our plans and deeds… We are God's: let us therefore live for him and die for him.
author: John Calvin

text: Faith is a firm and certain knowledge of God's benevolence toward us, founded upon the truth of the freely given promise in Christ, both revealed to our minds and sealed upon our hearts through the Holy Spirit.
author: John Calvin

text: Justification by faith… is the main hinge on which religion turns.
author: John Calvin

text: We see that our whole salvation and all its parts are comprehended in Christ.
author: John Calvin

text: Prayer… is the chief exercise of faith, and by which we daily receive God's benefits.
author: John Calvin
source: Institutes of the Christian Religion, 3.20 (chapter title)

text: Scripture, gathering up the otherwise confused knowledge of God in our minds, having dispersed our dullness, clearly shows us the true God.
author: John Calvin

text: As nurses commonly do with infants, God is wont in a measure to "lisp" in speaking to us.
author: John Calvin

text: Scripture is the school of the Holy Spirit, in which, as nothing is omitted that is both necessary and useful to know, so nothing is taught but what is expedient to know.
author: John Calvin

text: What is the chief end of human life? To know God by whom men were created.
author: John Calvin

text: When our Lord and Master Jesus Christ said, "Repent," he willed the entire life of believers to be one of repentance.
author: Martin Luther

text: The true treasure of the church is the most holy gospel of the glory and grace of God.
author: Martin Luther

text: The love of God does not find, but creates, that which is pleasing to it.
author: Martin Luther

text: A theologian of glory calls evil good and good evil. A theologian of the cross calls the thing what it actually is.
author: Martin Luther

text: A Christian is a perfectly free lord of all, subject to none. A Christian is a perfectly dutiful servant of all, subject to all.
author: Martin Luther

text: My conscience is captive to the Word of God.
author: Martin Luther

text: I did nothing; the Word did everything.
author: Martin Luther

text: Faith is a living, daring confidence in God's grace, so sure and certain that a man could stake his life on it a thousand times.
author: Martin Luther
source: Preface to the Epistle to the Romans (1522)

text: Our theology is certain: it snatches us away from ourselves and places us outside ourselves… on the promise and truth of God, which cannot deceive.
author: Martin Luther

text: That to which your heart clings and entrusts itself is, I say, really your God.
author: Martin Luther

text: And though this world, with devils filled, should threaten to undo us, we will not fear, for God hath willed his truth to triumph through us.
author: Martin Luther
source: "A Mighty Fortress Is Our God" (tr. F. H. Hedge)

text: We are beggars. This is true.
author: Martin Luther

text: You have made us for yourself, and our heart is restless until it rests in you.
author: Augustine of Hippo

text: Give what you command, and command what you will.
author: Augustine of Hippo

text: Late have I loved you, O Beauty ever ancient, ever new, late have I loved you!
author: Augustine of Hippo

text: Two cities have been formed by two loves: the earthly by the love of self, even to the contempt of God; the heavenly by the love of God, even to the contempt of self.
author: Augustine of Hippo

text: Love, and do what you will.
author: Augustine of Hippo
source: Homilies on the First Epistle of John, 7.8

text: For God's sake, do something brave!
author: Ulrich Zwingli

text: The preaching of the Word of God is the Word of God.
author: Heinrich Bullinger

text: It belongs in truth to the Church of God… to endure blows, not to strike them. But may it please you to remember that it is an anvil which has worn out many hammers.
author: Theodore Beza
source: To the King of Navarre, after the massacre at Vassy (1562)

text: What is your only comfort in life and in death? That I am not my own, but belong—body and soul, in life and in death—to my faithful Savior Jesus Christ.
author: Heidelberg Catechism

text: Three things: first, how great my sin and misery are; second, how I am set free from all my sins and misery; third, how I am to thank God for such deliverance.
author: Heidelberg Catechism

text: True faith is not only a sure knowledge by which I hold as true all that God has revealed to us in Scripture; it is also a wholehearted trust, which the Holy Spirit creates in me by the gospel.
author: Heidelberg Catechism

text: He is able to do this because he is almighty God and desires to do this because he is a faithful Father.
author: Heidelberg Catechism

text: All things, in fact, come to us not by chance but by his fatherly hand.
author: Heidelberg Catechism

text: Out of sheer grace, God grants and credits to me the perfect satisfaction, righteousness, and holiness of Christ, as if I had never sinned nor been a sinner.
author: Heidelberg Catechism

text: Because prayer is the most important part of the thankfulness God requires of us.
author: Heidelberg Catechism

text: We know him by two means: first, by the creation, preservation, and government of the universe, which is before our eyes as a most elegant book… Second, he makes himself more clearly and fully known to us by his holy and divine Word.
author: Belgic Confession

text: Man's chief end is to glorify God, and to enjoy him for ever.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: The Word of God, which is contained in the scriptures of the Old and New Testaments, is the only rule to direct us how we may glorify and enjoy him.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: God is a Spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable, in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness, and truth.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: There are three persons in the Godhead; the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost; and these three are one God, the same in substance, equal in power and glory.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: The decrees of God are his eternal purpose, according to the counsel of his will, whereby, for his own glory, he hath foreordained whatsoever comes to pass.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: God's works of providence are his most holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing all his creatures, and all their actions.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: Sin is any want of conformity unto, or transgression of, the law of God.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: The only Redeemer of God's elect is the Lord Jesus Christ, who, being the eternal Son of God, became man, and so was, and continueth to be, God and man in two distinct natures, and one person, for ever.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: Effectual calling is the work of God's Spirit, whereby, convincing us of our sin and misery, enlightening our minds in the knowledge of Christ, and renewing our wills, he doth persuade and enable us to embrace Jesus Christ, freely offered to us in the gospel.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: Justification is an act of God's free grace, wherein he pardoneth all our sins, and accepteth us as righteous in his sight, only for the righteousness of Christ imputed to us, and received by faith alone.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: Adoption is an act of God's free grace, whereby we are received into the number, and have a right to all the privileges of the sons of God.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: Sanctification is the work of God's free grace, whereby we are renewed in the whole man after the image of God, and are enabled more and more to die unto sin, and live unto righteousness.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: Assurance of God's love, peace of conscience, joy in the Holy Ghost, increase of grace, and perseverance therein to the end.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: The souls of believers are at their death made perfect in holiness, and do immediately pass into glory; and their bodies, being still united to Christ, do rest in their graves till the resurrection.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: At the resurrection, believers being raised up in glory, shall be openly acknowledged and acquitted in the day of judgment, and made perfectly blessed in the full enjoying of God to all eternity.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: Faith in Jesus Christ is a saving grace, whereby we receive and rest upon him alone for salvation, as he is offered to us in the gospel.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: Prayer is an offering up of our desires unto God, for things agreeable to his will, in the name of Christ, with confession of our sins, and thankful acknowledgment of his mercies.
author: Westminster Shorter Catechism

text: God alone is Lord of the conscience, and hath left it free from the doctrines and commandments of men, which are, in any thing, contrary to his Word; or beside it, if matters of faith, or worship.
author: Westminster Confession of Faith

text: Do you mortify; do you make it your daily work; be always at it whilst you live; cease not a day from this work; be killing sin or it will be killing you.
author: John Owen
source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers (1656), ch. 2

text: The greatest sorrow and burden you can lay upon the Father, the greatest unkindness you can do unto him, is not to believe that he loves you.
author: John Owen

text: No man shall ever behold the glory of Christ by sight hereafter, who doth not in some measure behold it by faith here in this world.
author: John Owen
source: Meditations on the Glory of Christ (1684)

text: There is more mercy in Christ than sin in us.
author: Richard Sibbes

text: Christ, the Scripture, your own hearts, and Satan's devices, are the four prime things that should be first and most studied and searched.
author: Thomas Brooks
source: Precious Remedies Against Satan's Devices (1652), to the reader

text: The greatest difficulty in conversion, is to win the heart to God; and the greatest difficulty after conversion, is to keep the heart with God.
author: John Flavel

text: Some providences, like Hebrew letters, must be read backward.
author: John Flavel

text: I preached as never sure to preach again, and as a dying man to dying men.
author: Richard Baxter

text: Take heed to yourselves, lest you should be void of that saving grace of God which you offer to others, and be strangers to the effectual working of that gospel which you preach.
author: Richard Baxter

text: He hath given me rest by his sorrow, and life by his death.
author: John Bunyan

text: In prayer it is better to have a heart without words, than words without a heart.
author: John Bunyan
source: I Will Pray with the Spirit (1662)

text: Grace groweth best in winter.
author: Samuel Rutherford

text: When I am in the cellar of affliction, I look for the Lord's choicest wines.
author: Samuel Rutherford

text: Christ and his cross are not separable in this life; howbeit Christ and his cross part at heaven's door.
author: Samuel Rutherford

text: If we had no winter, the spring would not be so pleasant: if we did not sometimes taste of adversity, prosperity would not be so welcome.
author: Anne Bradstreet

text: Resolved, to live with all my might, while I do live.
author: Jonathan Edwards

text: Resolved, never to do anything, which I should be afraid to do, if it were the last hour of my life.
author: Jonathan Edwards

text: The enjoyment of God is the only happiness with which our souls can be satisfied.
author: Jonathan Edwards

text: There is a difference between having an opinion that God is holy and gracious, and having a sense of the loveliness and beauty of that holiness and grace.
author: Jonathan Edwards

text: True religion, in great part, consists in holy affections.
author: Jonathan Edwards

text: God is glorified not only by his glory's being seen, but by its being rejoiced in.
author: Jonathan Edwards

text: Heaven is a world of love.
author: Jonathan Edwards

text: My memory is nearly gone; but I remember two things: that I am a great sinner, and that Christ is a great Saviour.
author: John Newton
source: Spoken late in life, recorded by William Jay

text: 'Twas grace that taught my heart to fear, and grace my fears relieved.
author: John Newton

text: Nothing in my hand I bring, simply to thy cross I cling.
author: Augustus Toplady

text: Love so amazing, so divine, demands my soul, my life, my all.
author: Isaac Watts

text: The only way to dispossess the heart of an old affection, is by the expulsive power of a new one.
author: Thomas Chalmers
source: The Expulsive Power of a New Affection

text: For every look at self, take ten looks at Christ.
author: Robert Murray M'Cheyne

text: My people's greatest need is my personal holiness.
author: Robert Murray M'Cheyne

text: If I could hear Christ praying for me in the next room, I would not fear a million of enemies. Yet distance makes no difference. He is praying for me.
author: Robert Murray M'Cheyne

text: Not what my hands have done can save my guilty soul; not what my toiling flesh has borne can make my spirit whole.
author: Horatius Bonar

text: Not what I am, O Lord, but what thou art; that, that alone can be my soul's true rest.
author: Horatius Bonar

text: Prayer and sin will never live together in the same heart. Prayer will consume sin, or sin will choke prayer.
author: J. C. Ryle

text: We must be holy, because this is one grand end and purpose for which Christ came into the world.
author: J. C. Ryle

text: There is no attribute more comforting to his children than that of God's Sovereignty.
author: Charles Spurgeon

text: If sinners be damned, at least let them leap to hell over our bodies.
author: Charles Spurgeon

text: Nobody ever outgrows Scripture; the book widens and deepens with our years.
author: Charles Spurgeon

text: There is not a square inch in the whole domain of our human existence over which Christ, who is Sovereign over all, does not cry: "Mine!"
author: Abraham Kuyper

text: Mystery is the lifeblood of dogmatics.
author: Herman Bavinck

text: The Christian movement at its inception was not just a way of life in the modern sense, but a way of life founded upon a message.
author: J. Gresham Machen

text: I'm so thankful for the active obedience of Christ. No hope without it.
author: J. Gresham Machen

text: Have you realized that most of your unhappiness in life is due to the fact that you are listening to yourself instead of talking to yourself?
author: D. Martyn Lloyd-Jones

text: What is preaching? Logic on fire! Eloquent reason!
author: D. Martyn Lloyd-Jones

text: What were we made for? To know God. What aim should we set ourselves in life? To know God.
author: J. I. Packer

text: What matters supremely, therefore, is not, in the last analysis, the fact that I know God, but the larger fact which underlies it—the fact that he knows me.
author: J. I. Packer

text: The essence of sin is man substituting himself for God, while the essence of salvation is God substituting himself for man.
author: John Stott

text: If there is one single molecule in this universe running around loose, totally free of God's sovereignty, then we have no guarantee that a single promise of God will ever be fulfilled.
author: R. C. Sproul
